headline: Teacher dies after falling from rickshaw during snatching near parliament
summary: Ranjina Parvin, a 55-year-old headteacher, was killed after snatchers on motorcycles pulled her bag, causing her to fall from her rickshaw.
details: A 55-year-old headteacher, Ranjina Parvin, died after falling from a rickshaw during a snatching incident near the National Parliament building's South Plaza.
The incident occurred around 6:30 AM on Saturday. Parvin had traveled from Bogura to Dhaka to visit a hospital in Farmgate.
According to reports, snatchers on motorcycles pulled her bag, causing her to fall from the rickshaw and sustain serious injuries.
She was rushed to Suhrawardy Hospital, where the duty doctor declared her dead.
Police are currently working to identify and arrest the suspects involved in the incident.
caption:
A headteacher dies after being pulled from a rickshaw by snatchers near the National Parliament building.

A 55-year-old headteacher, Ranjina Parvin, died after falling from a rickshaw during a snatching incident near the National Parliament building's South Plaza.

The incident occurred around 6:30 AM on Saturday. Parvin had traveled from Bogura to Dhaka to visit a hospital in Farmgate.

According to reports, snatchers on motorcycles pulled her bag, causing her to fall from the rickshaw and sustain serious injuries.

She was rushed to Suhrawardy Hospital, where the duty doctor declared her dead.

Police are currently working to identify and arrest the suspects involved in the incident.

headline: Up to Tk2 lakh reward for information on looted, illegal arms
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced a special police unit to recover stolen weapons and rewards for informants.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has announced the formation of a special unit to recover looted and illegal weapons across the country.
Informants providing information leading to the recovery of these arms will receive rewards ranging from Tk10,000 to Tk2 lakh.
The reward for heavy weapons is set at Tk2 lakh, while light weapons will fetch a reward of Tk50,000.
The Home Minister assured that the identities of those who provide information will be kept strictly confidential.
This announcement was made following a quarterly crime review meeting of law enforcement agencies at the Rajarbagh Police Auditorium on Saturday.
The Minister also stated that operations have already begun to arrest extortionists and terrorists nationwide.
He warned that police officers who fail to take appropriate action against extortionists and terrorists will face disciplinary measures.
caption:
Get up to Tk2 lakh for reporting looted or illegal weapons. The government is forming a special unit to recover them.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has announced the formation of a special unit to recover looted and illegal weapons across the country.

Informants providing information leading to the recovery of these arms will receive rewards ranging from Tk10,000 to Tk2 lakh.

The reward for heavy weapons is set at Tk2 lakh, while light weapons will fetch a reward of Tk50,000.

The Home Minister assured that the identities of those who provide information will be kept strictly confidential.

This announcement was made following a quarterly crime review meeting of law enforcement agencies at the Rajarbagh Police Auditorium on Saturday.

The Minister also stated that operations have already begun to arrest extortionists and terrorists nationwide.

He warned that police officers who fail to take appropriate action against extortionists and terrorists will face disciplinary measures.
